transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been feeling really down and depressed for a very long time now. It feels like this constant sadness has been hanging over me for about two years. I just haven't been able to shake this low mood.
Have there been any periods during these two years when you felt relatively better for more than two months at a time?
No, I really can't recall any periods where I felt significantly better or normal for that long. It feels like this heavy mood has just been constant without any real breaks over the last two years.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Major Depressive Disorder", "Persistent Depressive Disorder"], but based on this conversation, Major Depressive Disorder is less likely because the patient reports a constant low mood for two years without significant breaks, which aligns more closely with Persistent Depressive Disorder (dysthymia). The chronicity and absence of symptom-free intervals exceeding two months meet the diagnostic criteria for Persistent Depressive Disorder, making it the most appropriate candidate.
